Plant the Moon Experimental Design 
Team Name: SGMS RAD Force 
 
Team Number: 12617 
Rationale/Background: 
This project would help NASA with their research on growing food on the Moon. We choose 
radishes because they do not take long to grow and they will spice up the food people eat when 
they are on the Moon. 
Radishes grow best in light, sandy loams. They prefer well drained soils that are fertile and not 
compacted. They like temperatures that range from 40 – 50 degrees Fahrenheit, but 60 degrees is 
the best. 
Radishes are best eaten raw as a condiment or in sandwiches or salads. They can be added to 
soups. They have few calories and almost no fat. They are a good source of vitamin C. They 
contain antioxidants as well as calcium and potassium. Radish leaves can be harvested and eaten. 
Research Question: What helps plants grow in regolith? 
Independent Variable: The amount of miracle gro seed starter fertilizer mix used. 
Dependent Variable: The number and mass of the radishes. 
Controlled variables (constants): Size of pots, amount of regolith. 
Control group: The pots without miracle gro. 
Hypothesis: If the amount of miracle gro is increased than the radishes will grow bigger. 
Planting Design 
Crop: Southern Charm Radishes 
Experimental Design Procedures: 
1. Get out all materials 
2. Put together plant stand. 
3. Put on goggles, lab coat, mask, gloves 
4. Label pots with the percentage of each additive. 
5. Get the planting materials ready. 
6. Mix 50% regolith and 50% soil 
 50% regolith, 25% miracle gro, and 25% soil 
 50% regolith, 15% miracle gro, and 35% potting soil. 
7. Put 240 mL of the regolith mixtures in each labeled pot. 
8. Place two radish seeds in the north, south, east, and west of the pot and two in the center. 
9. Sprinkle additional regolith mixture on top to cover seeds. 
10. Place pots on wicking cloth covered trays. 
11. Water the seeds. Record the amount of water. 
11. Place the pots on trays and put them under the grow lights. 
12. Record observations.

Our results did not support our hypothesis. The radishes that grew with only 15% miracle gro 
grew the biggest. The radishes with the most miracle gro came in second and the no miracle 
grow radishes came in last. 
We were surprised by our results. Radishes even grew in regolith and potting soil. We think this 
was because the potting soil made the regolith less compact.

pages.text:
Some problems we encountered were with the watering. We were not good at taking turns and 
some of us forgot. We decided that three people would do the watering and it got better. We also 
used a mister to water the radishes because the leaves looked droopy. This made the plants look 
healthier. 
We were curious about how the radishes grew. The bulbs mostly sat on top of the potting mixture 
and did not grow under the soil like most root crops. If we were to do this experiment again, we 
would grow some radishes in only potting soil to see if they grow underground. 
We concluded that radishes would be a good crop to grow in lunar regolith. They would spice up 
the food for the astronauts so they would be less bored with the space food they have to eat. 
We learned how to grow a plants better and have been able to keep everything alive and in good 
condition.
